title: ADK Setup
text:
0.1 How to Use This Book
This short book walks you from a clean computer to a working Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) project. The focus stays on a simple path that works on macOS and Windows with the official Python installer and pip.

title: ADK Setup
text:
Move through the chapters in order. Each builds on the previous one.
Choose the operating system that matches your device when prompted.
Copy commands exactly as shown; they assume the official Python 3.11 installer.
Keep a notes file handy. Recording versions or paths now saves time later.







Tip: If you are setting up a managed or school laptop, confirm you can install software and modify your PATH before starting.

title: ADK Setup
text:
0.2 Why Python 3.11 and pip?
Python 3.11 is the current sweet spot for AI tooling: fast enough, broadly supported, and stable. Using the built-in venv module together with pip keeps the workflow lightweight, so you avoid extra package managers or community tooling until you need them.

title: ADK Setup
text:
0.3 What You Need

macOS 12+ or Windows 10/11 with administrator access
A browser and internet connection to download installers
A Google account and Gemini API key (created later in the setup)







No prior command-line experience is required. Every command is preceded by a short explanation, and checkpoints confirm that each step worked.



Continue with Preparation to learn the core ideas before installing anything.

title: Orientation
text:
Start Here
This orientation explains how the ADK Setup book flows and what you should expect from each part before diving into the hands-on steps.

title: Orientation
text:
How the Book Is Organised

Preparation (this part) — clarify terminology, requirements, and why Python 3.11 is the baseline.
Install Python — follow macOS or Windows instructions from python.org, no extra package managers required.
Build Your Workspace — create a virtual environment, install ADK, launch your first agent, and optionally wire up Jupyter.
Troubleshooting — look up fixes when a checkpoint fails.
Appendix — quick references, glossary, and official links.







Tip: Work through each chapter in order. When you hit an OS-specific section, complete the one that matches your machine, then jump back to the shared steps.

title: Orientation
text:
Checkpoints
Every chapter ends with a .callout-check that spells out what success looks like. If something does not match the expectation, open the Troubleshooting part and search for the symptom before moving on.

title: 2  Preparation
text: 2.1 Key Concepts in Plain Language

title: 2  Preparation
text:
Google Agent Development Kit (ADK): Google’s toolkit for building AI agents that can talk, reason, and take actions. You interact with it through commands like adk create.
Python: The programming language ADK uses. The guide standardises on Python 3.11 because it is stable and fully compatible with current ADK releases.
Virtual environment (venv): A self-contained folder that holds Python packages for a single project. It prevents updates in one project from breaking another.
pip: Python’s built-in package installer. You use it to add ADK and related libraries.
Gemini API key: A credential that lets ADK talk to Google’s Gemini models. You can create one later at https://ai.google.dev.

title: 2  Preparation
text:
2.2 Before You Continue

Make sure you can install software on your computer (admin or install permissions).
Have about 2 GB of free disk space.
Know whether you are using macOS or Windows. The next chapter sends you to the correct path.







If you are migrating from another Python version, keep it installed. The virtual environment will ensure the new setup does not conflict with existing work.

title: 2  Preparation
text:
2.3 Why Stick to Python 3.11?
Python 3.11 hits the balance between performance and compatibility:

ADK’s templates and dependencies target 3.11 by default.
Major libraries (NumPy, pandas, TensorFlow) publish pre-built wheels for 3.11, saving compilation time.
Python 3.12 or newer may work, but not all packages have caught up yet.







When downloading from python.org, record where the installer places python3.11. You will confirm the location during the verification step.

title: 2  Preparation
text:
2.4 Next Stop
Head to Python Installation and choose the chapter that matches your operating system.

title: Choose Your Python Path
text:
Pick the Right Instructions
The next chapters cover installing Python 3.11 with the official installers. Choose the chapter that matches your operating system and follow it start to finish.

title: Choose Your Python Path
text:
Installation Options



Operating System
What You Will Do
Start Here




macOS
Download the universal installer from python.org, run it, and confirm python3.11 is available in Terminal.
macOS — Python 3.11 via python.org


Windows
Download the 64-bit Windows installer from python.org, run it with the Add python.exe to PATH box checked, and confirm python points to 3.11.
Windows — Python 3.11 via python.org









Linux paths vary widely by distribution and package manager. If you need a Linux setup later, replicate the same philosophy: use your distribution’s Python 3.11 packages plus venv.

title: Choose Your Python Path
text:
Stay Consistent

Use the same target version (3.11.x) on every machine.
Avoid mixing installers. Do not combine the python.org installer with other package managers on the same computer.
When the installer offers the option to install pip and venv, keep it checked.

Continue to your operating system chapter now.

title: 3  title: “macOS — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text: 3.1 Step 1. Download the Installer

title: 3  title: “macOS — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
Open your browser to the official Python 3.11 release page: https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3110/
Scroll to Files and download the macOS 64-bit universal2 installer (.pkg).







Save the installer in your Downloads folder so you can remove it once the installation succeeds.

title: 3  title: “macOS — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
3.2 Step 2. Run the Installer

Double-click the downloaded .pkg.
Accept the license and proceed with the default options.
When prompted for admin approval, enter your password to allow the installation.







If macOS blocks the installer, right-click the .pkg, choose Open, then click Open again to bypass Gatekeeper for this trusted package.

title: 3  title: “macOS — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
3.3 Step 3. Verify the Installation
Open Terminal (Launchpad → search for “Terminal”) and run the following checks.

Confirm that Python 3.11 is reachable from the command line:

python3.11 --version

Confirm that pip is installed with the same interpreter:

pip3.11 --version

Expect outputs similar to Python 3.11.x and pip 24.x. If you see another version, retry the installer and ensure you launched the newly installed Terminal session.

title: 3  title: “macOS — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
3.4 Step 4. Create a Convenience Alias (Optional)
If the commands above work but you prefer to type python instead of python3.11, create a shell alias.

Open your shell profile in the default text editor:

open -e ~/.zprofile
Add this line at the end of the file, then save and close:
alias python="python3.11"
alias pip="pip3.11"

Reload the profile so the alias is available immediately:

source ~/.zprofile






The alias only affects new Terminal sessions. If you run automated scripts later, call python3.11 explicitly to avoid ambiguity.

title: 3  title: “macOS — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
3.5 Step 5. Record the Installation Path
Knowing where Python lives helps when configuring IDEs.

Print the full path to the Python 3.11 executable:

which python3.11
Take note of the path (usually /usr/local/bin/python3.11). You will reference it when creating virtual environments.
Once the checks pass, move on to Virtual Environment and pip.

title: 4  title: “Windows — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text: 4.1 Step 1. Download the Installer

title: 4  title: “Windows — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
In your browser, open https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3110/.
Under Files, download Windows installer (64-bit).







Do not run the installer from inside the ZIP preview. Save it to your Downloads folder first.

title: 4  title: “Windows — Python 3.11 via python.org”
section: 4.2 Step 2. Run the Installer with the Correct Options
text:
4.2 Step 2. Run the Installer with the Correct Options

Double-click python-3.11.x-amd64.exe.
At the bottom of the first screen, check the box labeled Add python.exe to PATH.
Click Customize installation. Keep all optional features checked.
On the next screen, ensure Install for all users is selected (requires admin rights) and confirm the install location (default is C:\Program Files\Python311\).
Click Install and let the setup finish.

If Windows SmartScreen warns you, choose More info → Run anyway.

title: 4  title: “Windows — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
4.3 Step 3. Verify the Installation
Open Windows Terminal or PowerShell (Win + X → Windows Terminal).

Confirm that Python 3.11 is active when calling python:

python --version

Confirm that pip is bundled with this interpreter:

pip --version

You should see Python 3.11.x and pip 24.x. If the version is different or the commands are missing, sign out and back in to refresh the PATH, then retry the checks.

title: 4  title: “Windows — Python 3.11 via python.org”
section: 4.4 Step 4. Enable Long Paths (Optional but Helpful)
text:
4.4 Step 4. Enable Long Paths (Optional but Helpful)
Some Python packages create nested folders. Enable long paths to avoid errors.

Turn on long path support via PowerShell:

Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem" `
  -Name "LongPathsEnabled" -Value 1
Restart Windows Terminal after running the command.

title: 4  title: “Windows — Python 3.11 via python.org”
text:
4.5 Step 5. Record the Installation Path

Print the directory where python.exe lives:

Get-Command python | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Source
Keep the path handy for IDE configuration (for example C:\Program Files\Python311\python.exe).
Proceed to Virtual Environment and pip once all checks pass.

title: 5  title: “Virtual Environment and pip”
text: 5.1 Why Use a Virtual Environment?

title: 5  title: “Virtual Environment and pip”
text:
Keeps ADK and its libraries separate from system Python.
Allows experiments without risking other projects.
Makes it easy to recreate the setup by sharing the commands.







Run the commands from the folder where you want to store your ADK projects, such as Documents/adk.

title: 5  title: “Virtual Environment and pip”
text:
5.2 macOS Terminal

Create a virtual environment named .venv using Python 3.11:

python3.11 -m venv .venv

Activate the environment (notice the (.venv) prefix in your prompt):

source .venv/bin/activate

Upgrade pip inside the activated environment:

python -m pip install --upgrade pip

title: 5  title: “Virtual Environment and pip”
text:
5.3 Windows PowerShell

Create the .venv folder using the Python 3.11 interpreter:

python -m venv .venv

Activate the environment for the current PowerShell session:

.\\.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1

Upgrade pip while the environment is active:

python -m pip install --upgrade pip

After activation, the prompt starts with (.venv) and python --version reports 3.11.x. If Activate.ps1 is blocked, set the execution policy using Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned and retry.

Stay inside the activated environment for the remaining setup steps.

title: 6  title: “Install Google ADK”
text:
6.1 Step 1. Confirm the Environment Is Active
Before installing, make sure you see (.venv) in your terminal prompt. If not, reactivate it:

title: 6  title: “Install Google ADK”
text:
Reactivate on macOS (zsh):

source .venv/bin/activate

Reactivate on Windows (PowerShell):

.\\.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1

title: 6  title: “Install Google ADK”
text:
6.2 Step 2. Install the ADK Package

Install the Google Agent Development Kit with pip:

pip install google-adk






The command above works on both macOS and Windows while the environment is active. pip automatically resolves compatible dependencies for Python 3.11.

title: 6  title: “Install Google ADK”
text:
6.3 Step 3. Verify the CLI

Confirm that the adk command is available:

adk --version

Expect a version string such as google-adk, version 0.x. If you see “command not found”, revisit the activation step—the CLI is installed inside .venv.

title: 6  title: “Install Google ADK”
section: 6.4 Step 4. Set the Gemini API Key
text:
6.4 Step 4. Set the Gemini API Key
You will need an API key from https://ai.google.dev. Once you have it, store it as an environment variable before creating projects.

6.4.1 macOS (zsh)

Add the key to your shell profile so it loads automatically:

echo 'export GEMINI_API_KEY="paste-your-key-here"' >> ~/.zprofile

Reload the profile to use the key immediately:

source ~/.zprofile


6.4.2 Windows (PowerShell)

Store the key for your user account:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("GEMINI_API_KEY","paste-your-key-here","User")

Load the new value into the current session:

$Env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "paste-your-key-here"






Treat the API key like a password. Never commit it to version control or share screenshots that display it.



Proceed to First Agent to scaffold your project.

title: 7  title: “Your First Agent”
text:
7.1 Step 1. Pick a Workspace Folder
Create or navigate to a folder where you want to store ADK projects (for example Documents/adk-projects). Keep the virtual environment active inside this folder path.

title: 7  title: “Your First Agent”
text: On macOS, use Finder → right-click → New Terminal at Folder. On Windows, open the folder in File Explorer, then type powershell in the address bar.

title: 7  title: “Your First Agent”
text:
7.2 Step 2. Create the Project

Scaffold a project named app_01 using the code agent template:

adk create --type=code app_01 --model gemini-2.0-flash-live-001 --api_key $GEMINI_API_KEY
What the parameters mean:

--type=code: Sets up a code-oriented agent.
app_01: Creates a folder with that name.
--model: Chooses the Gemini model for default prompts.
--api_key: Reads the key from the environment variable you stored earlier.







On Windows PowerShell, the same command works. If the API key does not populate, verify it with echo $Env:GEMINI_API_KEY first.

title: 7  title: “Your First Agent”
text:
7.3 Step 3. Explore the Project Layout

List the files that ADK generated:

ls app_01
You should see configuration files (such as adk.yaml) and starter code under app_01/src.

title: 7  title: “Your First Agent”
text:
7.4 Step 4. Start the Web Interface
Change into the project directory, then launch the ADK web UI.

Move into the project folder:

cd app_01

Start the local ADK web experience:

adk web

When the server starts, the terminal prints Serving on http://localhost:8000. Open that address in your browser to interact with the agent. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when finished.

title: 7  title: “Your First Agent”
text:
7.5 Step 5. Capture Your Settings
Record the following for future reference:

Python version (python --version)
ADK version (adk --version)
Location of the project folder

Having this information handy makes it easier to recreate the environment on a new machine.

title: 8  title: “Optional: Jupyter”
text:
8.1 When to Use Jupyter
If you only need the command-line interface, feel free to skip this chapter.

title: 8  title: “Optional: Jupyter”
text:
Prototype prompts or agent logic interactively.
Share notebooks with teammates while keeping dependencies identical.
Document experiments alongside runnable code.

title: 8  title: “Optional: Jupyter”
text:
8.2 Install Notebook Tools
Make sure the virtual environment is active ((.venv) in your prompt) before running these commands.

Install Jupyter and the IPython kernel helpers:

pip install jupyter ipykernel

Register the environment as a named kernel called adk-env:

python -m ipykernel install --user --name=adk-env

The second command prints the location of the new kernel. Open Jupyter (jupyter notebook or VS Code) and select adk-env to run notebooks inside this virtual environment.

title: 8  title: “Optional: Jupyter”
text:
8.3 Keep Things in Sync

Whenever you add packages with pip, they automatically become available inside the adk-env kernel.
If you rename the project folder, rerun the kernel registration command to update links.

To uninstall later, use jupyter kernelspec uninstall adk-env while the environment is active.

title: Troubleshooting Guide
text:
How to Use This Part
When something unexpected happens, start here. Each entry links a symptom to likely causes and simple fixes you can apply immediately.

title: Troubleshooting Guide
text:
Tips for Effective Troubleshooting

Re-run the verification command from the chapter where the problem appeared.
Capture the exact error message; even a single character matters.
If you are stuck, deactivate the virtual environment (deactivate), close the terminal, and repeat the last successful checkpoint.







Most installation issues trace back to an inactive virtual environment or a missing PATH entry. The tables in the next chapter point to the exact resolution steps.

title: 9  Common Errors
text: 9.1 adk: command not found

title: 9  Common Errors
text:
Likely Cause
Suggested Action




The virtual environment is inactive.
Activate it again using the command for your operating system.


adk was installed outside the environment.
Reinstall ADK while the environment is active.




Activate the environment on macOS:

source .venv/bin/activate

Reactivate the environment on Windows:

.\\.venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1

Reinstall ADK in the active environment if needed:

python -m pip install google-adk

title: 9  Common Errors
text:
9.2 python3.11: command not found (macOS)







Likely Cause
Fix




The installer was not run or Terminal is still using the old session.
Quit Terminal, reopen it, and rerun python3.11 --version.


PATH is missing /usr/local/bin.
Add export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH" to ~/.zprofile, then source ~/.zprofile.




Add /usr/local/bin to the PATH if needed:

echo 'export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zprofile

Reload the profile to apply the change:

source ~/.zprofile

title: 9  Common Errors
text:
9.3 pip Points to Another Python (Windows)







Likely Cause
Fix




Another Python version is earlier in PATH.
Use the interpreter to drive pip explicitly.




Invoke pip through Python 3.11:

python -m pip install --upgrade pip

title: 9  Common Errors
text:
9.4 TLS/SSL Errors During pip install







Likely Cause
Fix




Corporate SSL inspection or outdated certificates.
Install certificates bundled with Python.




Run the certificate installation script (macOS):

"/Applications/Python 3.11/Install Certificates.command"

Run the certificate installation script (Windows):

& "C:\Program Files\Python311\Install Certificates.command"
If the command path differs, open the Python installation folder and double-click the script manually.

title: 9  Common Errors
text:
9.5 ModuleNotFoundError After Activating the Environment







Likely Cause
Fix




Required package not installed in .venv.
Install the package while the environment is active.




Install a missing package (example for google-adk):

pip install google-adk






If you discover a new issue, add it to this chapter with the exact command and output. A future you (or teammate) will thank you.

title: Glossary
text:
Term
Plain-language meaning




ADK
Google Agent Development Kit, a toolkit for building AI assistants.


Agent
A software program that can reason about inputs and trigger actions (like calling APIs).


CLI
Command-line interface; you interact with ADK by typing commands.


Gemini
Google’s family of AI models used by ADK.


API key
A secret string that identifies you to Google’s services.


Python
The programming language ADK runs on.


Python 3.11
The specific Python release targeted in this guide.


Virtual environment (venv)
A folder that contains its own Python interpreter and packages.


pip
Python’s standard package manager for installing libraries.


PATH
An environment variable that tells your computer where to look for programs.


PowerShell
The default command-line shell included with Windows 10/11.


Terminal
The macOS application used to run shell commands.

title: 10  FAQ
text:
10.1 Why does the guide insist on Python 3.11?
ADK and most AI libraries ship precompiled wheels for Python 3.11. Earlier versions miss performance improvements; newer versions may not have all dependencies yet.

title: 10  FAQ
text:
10.2 Can I use Python 3.12 instead?
You can experiment with 3.12, but expect occasional package issues. If you need maximum compatibility, stick with 3.11 for now.

title: 10  FAQ
section: 10.3 Do I need to uninstall other Python versions first?
text:
10.3 Do I need to uninstall other Python versions first?
No. Multiple versions can coexist. Just make sure the virtual environment uses Python 3.11 and that you run commands inside the environment.

title: 10  FAQ
section: 10.4 Where do I get the Gemini API key?
text:
10.4 Where do I get the Gemini API key?
Visit https://ai.google.dev, sign in with your Google account, and create a key under Get API key. Store it securely using the commands shown in the ADK installation chapter.

title: 10  FAQ
section: 10.5 Can I work without the API key?
text:
10.5 Can I work without the API key?
You can create the project, but running the agent requires a valid key. Without it, ADK cannot contact Gemini models.

title: 10  FAQ
section: 10.6 Is Homebrew or another package manager required on macOS?
text:
10.6 Is Homebrew or another package manager required on macOS?
No. The instructions rely entirely on the python.org installer and pip. You can add Homebrew later if you need other development tools.

title: 10  FAQ
section: 10.7 How do I update ADK later?
text:
10.7 How do I update ADK later?
Activate your environment and run pip install --upgrade google-adk. Re-run adk --version afterwards to confirm the update.

title: 10  FAQ
section: 10.8 What if I accidentally installed packages outside the virtual environment?
text:
10.8 What if I accidentally installed packages outside the virtual environment?
Deactivate (deactivate), delete the .venv folder, recreate it with python3.11 -m venv .venv, and reinstall using the commands in the guide.
